artworks.title: Aeneas, Anchises, and Ascanius
artworks.description: Early marble group by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, commissioned by Cardinal Scipione Borghese and still in the Galleria Borghese, Rome. Aeneas carries his aged father Anchises out of burning Troy while the boy Ascanius follows behind — three generations of the Trojan house stacked into a single spiralling column of flight.

artworks.title: Aeneas' Flight from Troy
artworks.description: Oil painting by Federico Barocci in the Galleria Borghese, Rome, a second version of a composition first painted for Emperor Rudolf II and now lost. Aeneas bears Anchises on his shoulders through the burning city, with his son Ascanius beside him and his wife Creusa behind — the family's desperate escape from the sack of Troy.

artworks.title: Aeneas Tells Dido of the Misfortunes of Troy
artworks.description: Oil painting by Pierre-Narcisse Guérin, now in the Musée du Louvre, Paris. In a scene from the opening books of Virgil's Aeneid, the Trojan hero recounts the fall of his city to Dido, queen of Carthage, as evening falls over her court — the telling that kindles the queen's fatal love.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix cycle keeps Aeneas in the burning city — Aphrodite's son gathering the remnant that will, offscreen, become Rome.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's epic gives Aeneas his Virgilian exit: the survivor who walks out of the sack carrying the future.

music.title: Dido and Aeneas
music.description: Purcell's chamber opera for a girls' school ends with Dido's lament as Aeneas sails for Italy — the Trojan's duty staged as the cruelest courtesy in English music.

music.title: Les Troyens
music.description: Berlioz's vast Virgilian opera follows Aeneas from the fall of Troy to Dido's pyre — the hero of the Aeneid given a five-hour voice of brass and lament.
